title: Common neighbour conjectures for Saxl graphs fail at every base size
summary: For a finite permutation group, a base is a set of points with trivial pointwise stabiliser, and the generalised Saxl graph records which pairs of points lie together in a base of minimum size. Burness and Giudici conjectured that any two vertices of the Saxl graph of a primitive group of base size two have a common neighbour, and Freedman, Huang, Lee and Rekvényi extended this conjecture to arbitrary base size.
